Policy and Procedures on Student Mobility of the autonomous organization of education 
"Nazarbayev University"  
 
 
Section 1. Purpose and Application 
 
1.1. These Policy and Procedures on Student Mobility of the autono mous 
organization of education “ Nazarbayev University ” (hereinafter referred to as the 
Policy and  Procedures) establishes general principles and procedures for Student 
Mobility at the autonomous organization of education “Nazarbayev University”.  
1.2. These Policy and Procedure s apply to all students participating in 
mobility programs, both incoming and outgoing. The Policy and Procedure s are  
intended for the use by students, academic and administrative staff involved in the 
implementation of Student Mobility.   
 
Section 2. Terms / Definitions  
 
2.1. These Policy and Procedures use the following terms and definitions: 
1) Academic Exchange is in-person or online academic study and/or research 
experience (credit-bearing) that a student is undertaking at the Host Institution for a 
period of time (semester  or academic year), under the condition of the possibility of 
transfer of credits, waiver of tuition and corresponding expenses in case a Host 
institution is a Partner institution; 
2) Academic Mobility is i n-person or online academic experience that a 
student is undertaking at the Host Institution for a period of time (up to one academic 
year), which was formally approved and supported by his/her Home Institution (with 
written confirmation) on a free or fee -paying basis with the possibilitie s of credit 
transfer. Academic M obility can be presented in the following forms: Academic 
Exchange, Study Abroad Program, Overseas Component and Customized Program; 
3) Cultural Program is in-person or online short-term cultural exploration 
visit abroad. Students visit the  Host Institution on a reciprocal or non -reciprocal 
basis. Subject to agreement , Cultural programs developed jointly with Partner 
institutions can involve mutual waiver of corresponding expenses;  
4) Customized Program is a non-degree courses or courses over any semester 
or up to one year on a fee basis with the possibility for subsequent transfer of credits 
to their Home Institution taken by students and other individuals. It is not obligatory 
to be a degree -seeking student t o participate in the program, however, applicants 
should meet general admission criteria and meet other eligibility crit eria as indicated 
in items 3.5.1 . and 3.6.1. of the Policy  and Procedures  or as stated in the inter -
institutional agreement; 
5) Equivalent grade is NU equivalent of the grade received by an Outgoing 
student at the Host Institution, which is calculated by the School;  
6) Exchange Student  is a  student attending one of the Student Mobility 
programs for a certain period of time (up to one academic year), while pursuing a full 
academic degree at a Home Institution under the condition of transfer of credits with 
a waiver of tuition and corresponding expenses; 
7) Home Institution is higher education institution where a student is pursuing 
a full academic degree;

Section 3. Main Provisions 
3.1. General Regulations 
 
3.1.1. NU is committed to equality of opportunities and merit -based selection 
of students. Mobility programs are available to all student s, regardless of funding 
source or citizenship. Participation in various types of Student Mobility is subject to 
meeting eligibility  criteria stated in items  3.5.1. and 3.6.1. of th ese Policy and 
Procedures and conditions of particular types of Student Mobility.  
3.1.2. Student Mobility is organized in accordance with inter -institutional 
or/and inter-governmental agreements  and other relevant  documents (fee-based 
contract with Partner Institution or fee-based agreement with individual applicant).  
3.1.3. NU may consider full or partial funding of Student Mobility on a case –
by–case basis depending on the availability of funds at NU Schools.  
3.1.4. Issues not regulated by these Policy and Procedures shall be reviewed in 
accordance with the decision of the Academic Council and/or internal documents of 
NU. 
3.1.5. NU recognizes the value of Student Mobility to the overall academic, 
professional, cultural, and personal d evelopment of students. Student Mobility 
experiences offer NU students various opportunities, including expanding their 
academic learning, developing cultural and global competencies that contribute to 
their acquisition of NU graduate attributes, enriching  their professional learning and 
skills, enhancing personal development encompassing leadership abilities, social 
awareness, and global citizenship, and ultimately improving their employment 
prospects. 
3.1.6. NU offers a range of Student Mobility experiences, listed in item 3.1.9. 
of these Policy  and Procedures , offered by NU Schools, Partner Institutions, or 
independent providers. Students may also find opportunities for mobility outside of 
those provided by N U.  In such cases, NU Schools has the right whether or not to 
approve or recognize those opportunities based on the principles and rules in these 
Policy and Procedures. 
3.1.7. Providing students with opportunities for academically relevant mobility 
experiences as part of their study is an additional incentive opportunity provided by 
NU. 
3.1.8. In cases where credits earned at a Host Institution are transferred and 
counted toward degree completion at NU, this must be done in accordance with these 
Policy and Procedures.

academic year) with subsequent trans fer of credits on the basis of reciprocal waivers 
of tuition, application and registration fees . O ther possible corresponding expenses

partners, coordination of mobility process  for incoming masters and doctoral students 
and post-doctoral scholars.

3.4. Establishment and Implementation of Student Mobility 
 
3.4.1. If the participation of NU students in Student Mobility at the Host 
Institution is funded or co-funded by NU, the establishment of an inter -institutional 
agreement on the Mobility program between NU or NU Schools and the Host 
University is required , excluding Cultural Mobility which can be organized within 
MoU.e  
3.4.2. Inter-institutional agreements with the Partner Institution should include 
information on housing arrangements, payment of fees, support offered to students, 
risk management p rocedures, supervision and student management, academic 
content, and the process for establishing and maintaining the academic credit of the 
programs. Inter-institutional agreements shall be signed by the authorized person.  
3.4.3. Partner Institutions for Academi c Exchange or Study abroad program 
shall be considered and approved by the Academic Council if there is an absence of 
signed MoU with NU. Partner Institutions shall meet one of the criteria listed below. 
DI is responsible for verifying that the Partner Ins titution meets one of the following 
criteria: 
1) For Kazakhstani Institutions: 
Kazakhstan accreditation agencies included into the European Quality 
Assurance Register for Higher Education; 
Institutions with English as the main language of instruction (preferred); 
Members of alliances and associations NU is part of;  
2) International Institutions that meet one of the following criteria:  
To be ranked in the top 500 list of Times Higher Education World University 
Ranking, or Academic Ranking of World Universi ties, or QS World University 
Ranking agencies (ranking for the last 3 years should be considered);  
To be ranked in the top 300 in a subject area by the abovementioned ranking 
agencies. In this case, only the NU School from the matching area can send/host 
students (ranking for the last 3 years should be considered);  
The exchange agreement is supported by the Erasmus+ program or other 
programs funded by the governments; 
Participants and members of the Ivy League (the US), the Russel Group (the 
UK), and the C9 League (China); 
Highly specialized universities; 
Leading universities located in Eurasia; 
Leading universities ranked by the national ranking agencies;
